eyereach: The range or reach of the eye; eyeshot. "A seat in eyereach of him." B. Jonson.
eyewitness: One who sees a thing done; one who has ocular view anything. We . . . were eyewitnesses of his majesty. 2 Pet. i. 16.
eyeball: The ball or globe of the eye.
eyesplice: A splice formed by bending a rope's and back, and fastening it into the rope, forming a loop or eye. See Illust. under Splice.
eyesore: Something offensive to the eye or sight; a blemish. Mordecai was an eyesore to Haman. L'Estrange.
eyebar: A bar with an eye at one or both ends.
eyelet: 1. A small hole or perforation to receive a cord or fastener, as in garments, sails, etc. 2. A metal ring or grommet, or short metallic tube, the ends of which can be bent outward and over to fasten it in place; -- used to line an eyelet hole. Eyelet hole, a hole made for an eyelet.
eyeful: Filling or satisfying the eye; visible; remarkable. (old) "Eyeful trophies." Chapman.
eyestalk: One of the movable peduncles which, in the decapod Crustacea, bear the eyes at the tip.
eyebolt: A bolt which a looped head, or an opening in the head.
eyasmusket: An unfledged or young male sparrow hawk. (old) Shak.
eyecup: A small oval porcelain or glass cup, having a rim curved to fit the orbit of the eye. it is used in the application of liquid remedies to eyes; -- called also eyeglass.
eyelid: The cover of the eye; that portion of movable skin with which an animal covers or uncovers the eyeball at pleasure.
eyas: A nesting or unfledged Lird; in falconry, a young hawk from the nest, not able to pr Shak J. H. Walsh | Unfledged, or newly fledged. (old) Like eyas hawk up mounts unto the skies, His newly budded pinions assay. Spebser.
eyebeam: A glance of the eye. Shak.
eyestring: The tendon by which the eye is moved. Shak.
ey: an interj. of wonder or inquiry. (old) Chaucer.
eyespot: (a) A simple visual organ found in many invertebrates, consisting of pigment cells covering a sensory nerve termination. (b) An eyelike spot of color.
eyehole: A circular opening to recive a hook, cord, ring, or rope; an eyelet.
eyebrow: The brow or hairy arch above the eye. Shak.
eyespotted: Marked with spots like eyes. Junno's bird, in her eye-spotted train. Spenser.
eyra: A wild cat (Felis eyra) ranging from southern Brazil to Texas. It is reddish yellow and about the size of the domestic cat, but with a more slender body and shorter legs.
eyepiece: The lens, or combination of lenses, at the eye end of a telescope or other optical instrument, through which the image formed by the mirror or object glass is viewed. Collimating eyepiece. See under Collimate.
eyrie: The nest of a bird of prey or other large bird that builds in a lofty place; aerie. The eagle and the stork On cliffs and cedar tops their eyries build. Milton.
eyeservice: Service performed only under inspection, or the eye of an employer. Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers. Col. iii. 22.
eye: A brood; as, an eye of pheasants. | 1. The organ of sight or vision. In man, and the vertebrates generally, it is properly the movable ball or globe in the orbit, but the term often includes the adjacent parts.
eyelash: 1. The fringe of hair that edges the eyelid; -- usually in the pl. 2. A hair of the fringe on the edge of the eyelid.
eyesaint: An object of interest to the eye; one wirehaired with the eyes. (old) That's the eye-saint, I know, Among young gallants. Beau. & Fl.
eyot: A little island in a river or lake. See Ait. [Written also ait, ayt, eey, eyet, and eyght.] Blackstone.
eyeflap: A blinder on a horse's bridle.
eyeglass: 1. A lens of glass to assist the sight. Eyeglasses are used singly or in pairs. 2. Eyepiece of a telescope, microscope, etc. 3. The retina. (poetic) 4. A glass eyecup. See Eyecup.
eyalet: Formerly, one of the administrative divisions or provinces of the Ottoman Empire; -- now called a vilayet.
eyeleteer: A small, sharp-pointed instrument used in piercing eyelet holes; a stiletto.
eyebright: A small annual plant (Euphrasia officinalis), formerly much used as a remedy for diseases of the eye.
eyre: A journey in circuit of certain judges called justices in eyre (or in itinere). Note: They were itinerant judges, who rode the circuit, holding courts in the different counties.
eyestone: 1. A small, lenticular, calcareous body, esp. an operculum of a small shell of the family Tubinid, used to remove a foreign sub stance from the eye. It is rut into the inner corner of the eye under the lid, and allowed to work its way out at the outer corner, bringing with the substance. 2. (Min.) Eye agate. See under Eye.
eyen: Plural of eye; obsolete, or used only in poetry. Shak. With such a plaintive gaze their eyne Are fastened upwardly on mine. Mrs. Browning.
eyry: The nest of a bird of prey or other large bird that builds in a lofty place; aerie. The eagle and the stork On cliffs and cedar tops their eyries build. Milton.
eyesight: Sight of the eye; the sense of seeing; view; observation. Josephus sets this down from his own eyesight. Bp. Wilkins.
eyewater: A wash or lotion for application to the eyes.
eyeminded: Having one's mental imagery prevailingly of the visual type; having one's thoughts and memories mainly in the form of visual images. -- Eye"-mind`ed*ness, n.
eyne: Plural of eye; obsolete, or used only in poetry. Shak. With such a plaintive gaze their eyne Are fastened upwardly on mine. Mrs. Browning.
eyetooth: A canine tooth of the upper jaw. See Teeth. To cut one's eyeteeth, to become acute or knowing. [Colloq.]
eyeshot: Range, reach, or glance of the eye; view; sight; as, to be out of eyeshot. Dryden.
eyeopener: That which makes the eyes open, as startling news or occurrence, or (U. S. Slang), a drink of liquor, esp. the first one in the morning.
eyed: Heaving (such or so many) eyes; -- used in composition; as sharp-eyed; dull-eyed; sad-eyed; ox-eyed Juno; myriad-eyed.
eyeservant: A servant who attends faithfully to his duty only when watched.
